lens:
PATENT prior-art sweep for WS8 candidate S3 (tandem split: axle A = diesel through ONE fixed ratio with a rev-matched clutch, no change-speed gearbox anywhere on a 36,300 kg Class 8 combination; axle B = disconnectable e-axle owning launch, low speed, regen and peak assist; engine downsized toward cruise-plus-margin).

METHOD AND HARD CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE QUALITY. This environment's egress proxy refused CONNECT to every patent full-text host: patents.google.com, worldwide.espacenet.com, www.freepatentsonline.com, image-ppubs.uspto.gov, patents.justia.com, www.lens.org, api.patentsview.org, developer.uspto.gov and ped.uspto.gov all returned 403 connect_rejected to both WebFetch and curl (verified via the agent-proxy status endpoint). The ONLY working channel was server-side WebSearch, which returns titles, URLs and a synthesised summary. CONSEQUENCE: no independent-claim text below was read verbatim. Every "claim substance" statement is a paraphrase reconstructed from search-engine summaries of the patent page, and assignees/dates are as reported by those summaries. Under the program's own R2/R14 verbatim discipline this sweep is NOT claim-verified and must be treated as a lead list, not a freedom-to-operate opinion. Any S3 go/no-go that depends on claim scope needs a re-run with patent-database access, or outside counsel.

HEADLINE: S3's two constituent ideas are each thoroughly occupied, but at different scales, and NO document was found that occupies them JOINTLY at Class 8 scale. (a) "Engine to wheels through a fixed ratio with no variable-ratio transmission, electric machine owns launch and low speed, engine owns steady-state cruise and is sized for cruise efficiency" is the core of US5343970 (Severinsky/Paice, filed 1992, EXPIRED) and is re-expressed by Audi US9663101 and by US8695738 — all on light vehicles. (b) "Tandem split: engine drives one rear axle, electric machine drives the other" is occupied at heavy-duty scale by BAE US8875819, by the Dana distributed-drivetrain family, by the Hyliion TTR family, and was already recited as KNOWN prior art in EP0492152A1 (1991). In every heavy-duty instance of (b) the engine path retains a multi-ratio transmission. The junction of (a) and (b) on a 36 t combination is open ground — and the same search shows why: the heavy-duty art actively teaches away from one ratio.

items.name: US5343970A — Hybrid electric vehicle (Severinsky; later Paice LLC / Abell Foundation)
items.what_it_claims: ICE + traction motor + starter motor + battery under microprocessor control such that the engine is run ONLY under high-efficiency conditions (typically load >= ~30% of engine max torque); electric motor alone drives the vehicle at low speed and in traffic, both sources during acceleration and hill climbing, and the ENGINE ALONE during steady-state highway cruising, with the engine sized to sit at or near best efficiency at cruise. Per the specification the engine is coupled to the wheels at a FIXED RATIO with NO variable-ratio transmission — 'no transmission is employed' — torque from both sources joining at a controllable torque transfer unit. Filed 1992-09-21; granted 1994-09-06; EXPIRED (term ran out ~2012-13). Famously asserted against Toyota (jury infringement finding on two claims; Toyota settled 2010).
items.architecture: Single-axle parallel hybrid, engine on a fixed ratio, no gearbox; motor-launch / engine-cruise split (light vehicle)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND (no numeric fuel result retrievable through the search channel)
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES the intellectual ground of S3's engine path and control law almost exactly — fixed ratio, no gearbox, e-machine owns launch, engine owns cruise, engine downsized to cruise efficiency — but on a passenger car and on ONE axle, not a tandem split, and not at 36.3 t. Because it is EXPIRED it is freedom-to-operate-neutral and is instead the single strongest NOVELTY obstacle to any S3 claim drafted at the concept level: S3's novelty must live in the tandem-split-plus-heavy-duty-scale combination, not in 'fixed ratio plus electric launch'.

items.name: Paice 'Hybrid vehicles' continuation family — US6209672, US6338391, US7104347, US7455134, US7520353, US7559388, US7597164, US8214097, US8630761, US9050972, US9463698, US9573585; EP2289750A1; CA2556195C
items.what_it_claims: Long continuation chain off the Severinsky disclosure, filings roughly 1999-2013. Recurring claim substance: run the engine only when road load exceeds a setpoint fraction of engine maximum torque; motor supplies low-speed and transient torque; battery state-of-charge arbitration. US6338391 adds a turbocharger activated only when load exceeds engine max torque for an extended period. Notably the family's own disclosure states that 'a two-speed transmission may further be provided, to further broaden the vehicle's load range.'
items.architecture: Parallel hybrid, engine fixed-ratio in the base embodiment, optional two-speed in later embodiments (light vehicle)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS-AND-PARTLY-OCCUPIES. The later members are the live end of the family and their setpoint-based engine-on logic is close to S3's 'engine owns cruise-plus-margin' policy. More important for WS8: this family is where the fixed-ratio idea's own authors conceded that ONE ratio was not enough and added a second — on a ~1.5 t car. See contradictions.

items.name: US8875819B2 — Hybrid drive system for hybrid electric vehicles (BAE Systems Controls Inc; inventors Muggeo, Matthews)
items.what_it_claims: Medium/heavy-duty hybrid drive in which the internal combustion engine is the PRIMARY source of motive power, coupled to the front-most axle and to a first drive shaft in mechanical communication with a MIDDLE drive axle; plus an electric motor and a clutch assembly with a second driveshaft in mechanical communication with the REAR-MOST drive axle. Filed 2010-03-01; granted 2014.
items.architecture: Heavy-duty tandem split — engine on the forward/middle drive axle, clutched electric motor on the rear-most drive axle (through-the-road within the tandem)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES S3's TOPOLOGY at heavy-duty scale: engine on one tandem axle, clutched electric machine on the other. This is the closest structural hit in the whole sweep. What it does NOT appear to do is delete the change-speed transmission from the engine path — the engine is described as the primary motive source in a conventional driveline sense. S3's distinguishing feature versus this reference is therefore ONLY the deletion of the gearbox and the reassignment of launch duty to the e-axle, which makes that deletion load-bearing for both novelty and physics.

items.name: Dana Heavy Vehicle Systems — WO2017100258A1 / US11001134 / US11639094 'Distributed drivetrain architectures for commercial vehicles with a hybrid electric powertrain and DUAL RANGE DISCONNECT AXLES'; and WO2017100115A1 / US10486521 (same family, without dual range)
items.what_it_claims: Hybrid drivetrain for commercial vehicles comprising a power source, a transmission and a TANDEM AXLE ASSEMBLY with a first and a second axle, where one of the transmission and the tandem axle assembly carries a first motor-generator in electrical communication with a battery. A 'hybrid tandem axle drive unit' comprising a planetary drive unit, first and second axle drive assemblies and a motor-generator engaged with a geared shaft of the inter-axle assembly of the second axle drive assembly, placeable in at least two modes including a low-torque single-axle mode. Priority 2015-12-07 and 2016-10-10; PCT/US2016/065285 filed 2016-12-07; US grants 2019, 2021 and 2023.
items.architecture: Commercial-vehicle hybrid with distributed drive across a tandem, motor-generator at the inter-axle, DUAL RANGE (two-speed) disconnect axles
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES the hybrid-tandem-axle-unit ground and the disconnect ground, from the largest heavy-axle supplier, with 2015 priority. Critically it also CONTRADICTS S3's premise in its own background: it frames commercial-vehicle drivetrain design as requiring both a low-speed high-torque mode and a high-speed low-torque mode, and Dana's answer is DUAL RANGE, i.e. more ratios, not fewer. A single fixed ratio is the opposite of this reference's teaching.

items.name: Hyliion through-the-road (TTR) family — US20180086227A1 and grants US10245972, US10596913, US10744888, US11833905, US12024029, US12319150 ('Trailer-based energy capture and management'); US10889288, US11046302, US11351979, US11932232 ('electric drive controller adaptation to TTR coupled primary engine' / 'supplemental electric drive with primary engine recognition'); US20240034298A1 (traction assistance). Inventors Healy, Sa, Culbertson, Schmidt, Richter
items.what_it_claims: TTR hybridisation: supplement the motive force of an UNMODIFIED primary drivetrain and fuel-fed engine with supplemental torque at one or more electrically powered drive axles, retrofit or factory. The electric drive controller runs an ECMS / adaptive-ECMS at the e-axle, following or estimating states of the primary drivetrain and engine WITHOUT participating in engine or primary-drivetrain control, and adapts to BSFC-type data for the specific paired engine; regen commanded off brake-line pressure; motor-generator alternately assists and recuperates from an on-board energy store. The traction-assistance filing predicts slip conditions along a route from vehicle and external/cloud data and reconfigures the electric drive powertrain accordingly.
items.architecture: P4 / through-the-road e-axle overlay on a conventional diesel + AMT driveline (6X4HE product lineage; also trailer-tandem and dolly variants)
items.quantified_result: Product-level, not claim-level: Hyliion states 30% total fuel-and-emissions saving from a blend of 15% hybrid drive axle + 12% APU + 3% aerodynamics — i.e. the DRIVE-AXLE hybrid share alone is ~15%, and that is against a full conventional truck, not per payload tonne-km. Treat as vendor marketing, not a measured fleet result.
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES S3's axle-B function and its control philosophy (e-axle owning regen and assist, engine untouched), and does so with an issued, actively prosecuted US portfolio. It emphatically does NOT occupy the gearbox deletion — the whole Hyliion premise is that the primary drivetrain, transmission included, is left alone. Hyliion is therefore the reference S3 must beat on numbers, and the ~15% drive-axle-only figure is the informal bar for 'is deleting the gearbox worth it'.

items.name: US9663101B2 / EP3263381-family — Drive device for a hybrid vehicle (Audi AG; inventor Boris Blasinski)
items.what_it_claims: Stated principle of the invention is to REDUCE OR AVOID the clutch that couples the internal combustion engine to the drive axle: because the electric machine is used to start the vehicle moving, the engine no longer has to be coupled to the drive axle for launch. A control unit is configured to operate the electric machine EXCLUSIVELY to start the vehicle up to a THRESHOLD SPEED at which the hybrid vehicle can then be driven by the internal combustion engine. Granted 2017-05-30.
items.architecture: Parallel hybrid, electric launch to a threshold speed, engine coupled only above it, clutch minimised (passenger car)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES S3's CONTROL LAW verbatim in substance — e-machine owns launch to a threshold, engine engages only above it — and does so in a 2010s-era live patent rather than the expired Severinsky. It is a passenger-car document and does not address a tandem split, 36 t adhesion, or grade hold. The exposure this creates for S3 is on the control claim, not the topology claim.

items.name: US9005077 — Method to reduce lash clunk in a hybrid electric vehicle (assignee NOT confirmed through the available channel; US grant 2015)
items.what_it_claims: Method of starting the ICE of a hybrid powertrain having a transmission with a SELECTABLE CLUTCH DEVICE that, when engaged, mechanically couples the engine to a first axle at a FIXED ENGINE-SPEED-TO-AXLE-SPEED RATIO: spin and fuel the engine such that the engine-speed-to-axle-speed ratio EXCEEDS the fixed ratio, then engage the selectable clutch device once that condition holds.
items.architecture: Fixed-ratio engine-to-axle path with rev-matched (over-speed-then-engage) clutch engagement
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES S3's REV-MATCHED CLUTCH ENGAGEMENT OF A FIXED-RATIO ENGINE DRIVE — this is the single closest hit on that specific element, and it is expressed in exactly S3's terms (fixed engine-speed-to-axle-speed ratio, engagement conditioned on the speed ratio). What is not present is heavy-duty scale, the tandem split, or use of a SECOND AXLE's e-machine to perform the matching and bridge the torque hole during engagement. S3 should assume the bare rev-match idea is taken and claim the cross-axle coordination instead.

items.name: EP0492152A1 — Hybridantrieb für Fahrzeuge (hybrid drive for vehicles), published ~1992
items.what_it_claims: Its own background recites as a KNOWN concept that 'the internal combustion engine with clutch and conventional change-speed gearbox acts on one axle of the vehicle and an electric machine acts directly on the other axle.'
items.architecture: Through-the-road / P4 two-axle split, recited as admitted prior art
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: Most useful single FTO fact in the sweep: the through-the-road topology — engine on one axle, electric machine directly on the other — was already ADMITTED PRIOR ART in a European filing around 1991. Nobody can hold the bare topology. It also sharpens the point that the conventional version of that topology explicitly keeps the change-speed gearbox on the engine axle; S3's departure is the deletion, and only the deletion.

items.name: EP0812720A1 / EP0812720B1 — Vehicle with electric drive (published 1997-12-17; B1 2001-12-19)
items.what_it_claims: Commercial vehicle (agricultural/industrial tractor emphasis) with an engine-driven generator and at least one axle whose two wheels are driven by electric motors; the hybrid improvement has the IC engine also drive a shaft to that axle, with a SUMMING GEARBOX at each wheel combining shaft power and motor power. Related disclosure: at least one SECOND drive axle of the commercial vehicle can be driven purely mechanically in conventional fashion, connected to the internal combustion engine via a drive shaft and a SWITCHABLE (change-speed) TRANSMISSION.
items.architecture: Commercial-vehicle multi-axle hybrid; one axle electric/summed, a second axle mechanically engine-driven through a shiftable gearbox
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS. Same split-axle commercial-vehicle picture as S3, twenty-nine years earlier — and it explicitly keeps a switchable transmission on the engine-driven axle. It is a clean example of the pattern the whole sweep shows: heavy-vehicle split-drive art consistently retains the gearbox on the engine path.

items.name: US5947855A — Vehicle hybrid wheel drive system (Deere-family disclosure)
items.what_it_claims: Engine-driven drive shaft coupled to a first drive axle; a pair of summing gears, each with one input from the drive shaft and one from a respective electric motor (motors fed by an engine-driven generator), each summing gear output going through a final planetary speed-reducing gear to a wheel. Described as having a final drive with a high-speed reduction ratio for commercial vehicles.
items.architecture: Mechanically-summed series-parallel wheel drive on a commercial vehicle, fixed final reduction
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS. Fixed final reduction on a working commercial vehicle with electric torque summed in at the wheel — S3 splits the same two torque sources by AXLE rather than summing them at each wheel. Relevant as the mechanical alternative to S3's through-the-road split.

items.name: WO2019165167A1 — Torque control during gear shift for an electrically all-wheel drive hybrid vehicle (Scania-family; published 2019)
items.what_it_claims: A transmission transfers drive torque from a first torque-generating unit to ONLY a first axle. A controller decides to perform a gear shift and, WHILE shifting, controls a SECOND torque-generating unit — which drives ONLY a different second axle — to temporarily increase its torque and compensate the disturbance (the temporary reduction of drive torque at the first axle) caused by the shift.
items.architecture: eAWD heavy-vehicle hybrid; cross-axle electric torque-fill during a gear shift on the engine axle
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES 'electric torque-fill delivered across the axle split'. It is the nearest expression of S3's assist logic in a heavy-vehicle context — but it PRESUPPOSES the gearbox exists and only patches its shift holes. S3's premise is the strict complement: delete the gearbox so there is no hole to fill, and use the e-axle for the ratio range instead of the shift interruption. That complement is not claimed here.

items.name: Electric torque-fill cluster — US6629026B1; US20110168469A1; US20130296127A1; EP2490909A1; DE10163382A1
items.what_it_claims: US6629026B1: post-transmission parallel hybrid in which the motor supplies torque fill DIRECTLY to a drive axle via the differential while the engine is torsionally isolated by a shift. US20110168469A1: torque-fill during gear change on manual transmissions with dual propulsion sources, with motor torque reduced as the clutch re-transmits engine torque. US20130296127A1: torque-hole filling during automatic transmission shifting via a machine between engine and transmission. EP2490909A1: electric motors filling torque during an AMT shift interrupt to smooth the drive. DE10163382A1: hybrid control giving first priority to the electric drive when torque must be reduced for a gear change.
items.architecture: P2/P3/P4 electric torque-fill across a shift event
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES the electric-torque-fill-substituting-for-shift-quality ground densely and from many directions. All of it assumes a shifting transmission is present. None of it teaches that torque fill can substitute for the RATIOS THEMSELVES on a 36 t combination — that substitution is S3's actual claim and it is not made anywhere in this cluster.

items.name: US7470215 — Vehicle drivetrain with secondary clutch (granted 2008)
items.what_it_claims: A SINGLE-SPEED off-road vehicle with an engine and at least one driven wheel, and a transmission that selectively transfers torque from engine to driven wheel at a CONSTANT RATIO, comprising a first clutch driven by the engine and configured to AUTOMATICALLY ENGAGE ABOVE A THRESHOLD ENGINE SPEED, plus a normally-engaged second clutch that disengages above a threshold slip torque.
items.architecture: Constant-ratio engine drive with speed-threshold automatic clutch engagement, no change-speed gearbox (light off-road vehicle, non-hybrid)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS closely on the mechanism: fixed ratio engine to wheel, clutch engaging on an engine-speed threshold, no gearbox. Differs on everything that makes S3 hard — light vehicle, no hybrid, no electric launch partner, no 36 t grade hold. Useful as evidence that 'fixed ratio + speed-threshold clutch' as a bare mechanism is old.

items.name: US8695738 — Constant-ratio independent series-parallel hybrid drivetrain for a plug-in electric vehicle (granted 2014)
items.what_it_claims: Removes the transmission and uses a CONSTANT GEAR RATIO (example given ~10:1) to power the vehicle at highway speeds, achievable by belts, spur, helical or cog gears; the electric motor/generator needs no transmission because its inverter gives torque from zero rpm to a limit, and the constant-ratio gearbox multiplies power to the wheels without materially hurting drivetrain efficiency.
items.architecture: Constant-ratio series-parallel PHEV, transmission deleted
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES the 'delete the transmission, use one constant ratio, let the electric machine cover the low end' argument as a general drivetrain proposition — including the exact efficiency rationale S3 uses. Light vehicle; no tandem split; no rev-matched clutch. Together with US5343970 this means S3 cannot claim the reasoning, only the heavy-duty tandem embodiment of it.

items.name: US7338335B1 — Hybrid electric heavy-duty vehicle drive system (inventor Frank Messano; assignee listed as Individual; granted 2008)
items.what_it_claims: States that hybrid systems to cut fuel consumption for long-haul heavy-duty CLASS 8 trucks (and Class 4-7, motorhomes) were lacking, and proposes small, highly efficient CONSTANT-SPEED diesel engine-generators meeting varying speed and load demands, with road wheels driven by modular electrical motor suspension units.
items.architecture: Series diesel-electric Class 8, constant-speed genset, distributed wheel/suspension motors, no mechanical engine path
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS — it is Class 8 and it has no gearbox, but it gets there by going SERIES (S1's ground, not S3's). It is direct prior art against WS8's S1 rather than S3, and it is useful as the boundary marker: S3's whole point is keeping a mechanical cruise path that the series art throws away.

items.name: US8783396B2 — Hydrocarbon fueled-electric series hybrid propulsion systems (ePower Engine Systems LLC; assigned 2011-08-10; granted 2014-07-22)
items.what_it_claims: A Class 8 DOT vehicle hybrid propulsion system: hydrocarbon-fuelled engine, AC generator driven by it, DC battery, AC/DC controller, and an AC traction motor in driving engagement with the powertrain — the motor shaft connected directly to the rear differential. The diesel is NOT directly linked to the transmission for mechanical drive power. Also contemplates a SECONDARY traction motor, controller and secondary axle integrated into an integrated ELECTRIC AXLE.
items.architecture: Series diesel-electric Class 8; secondary e-axle contemplated
items.quantified_result: Specification asserts 50% or even 65%+ decrease in fuel usage versus conventional Class 8 DOT vehicles, and cites conventional Class 8 driveline efficiency of 38% or less and ~5.5 mpg baseline. These are unverified specification assertions, not measured fleet data — the real-world ePower retrofit was reported around 30%.
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS S3's axle-B and contradicts nothing directly, but its headline fuel numbers are the kind of unverified specification claim WS8 must NOT calibrate against. Its practical note that the shipping kit still included an automatic transmission from a major manufacturer is itself informative about how hard the no-gearbox path is in practice.

items.name: DE102016006206A1 / EP3246188A1 — Nutzfahrzeug mit einem Parallel-Hybrid-Antriebsstrang (commercial vehicle with a parallel hybrid drive train; MAN Truck & Bus lineage; filed 2016)
items.what_it_claims: Truck with a ladder frame of two longitudinal members and cross members, carrying a parallel hybrid powertrain: the internal combustion engine is drivingly connected to an axle via a MAIN transmission and an ADAPTATION transmission, with at least one motor-generator arranged on the adaptation transmission and connectable to the axle through it; the main transmission reaches the axle through two consecutive cardan shafts coupled by the adaptation transmission, which has a pass-through carrying engine torque from the first cardan shaft to the second.
items.architecture: P3-style driveline-mounted e-machine on a heavy truck, main change-speed gearbox retained
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS. The 'matching/adaptation gear' language initially looks like a fixed-ratio engine path, but on reading it is an ADDITION alongside a retained main gearbox, not a replacement for it. Another instance of the heavy-duty pattern: electrify around the transmission, never instead of it.

items.name: CN115416473A — 一种多轴驱动混合动力系统及车辆 (multi-axle drive hybrid power system and vehicle; Zhonglian Hengtong Machinery Co Ltd; filed 2022-08-09, published 2022-12-02)
items.what_it_claims: Multi-axle hybrid system comprising a mechanical drive unit and an electric drive unit that can drive the vehicle independently or cooperatively, with mechanical-drive, hybrid-drive and pure-electric modes, aimed at heavy-duty engineering vehicles and framed around eliminating the need for a traditional transmission (无变速箱).
items.architecture: Heavy multi-axle split mechanical/electric drive, gearbox elimination as an explicit goal
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: CLOSEST NON-US NEIGHBOUR and the only document found that pairs HEAVY vehicle + multi-axle split + explicit gearbox elimination. Off-highway engineering-vehicle duty, not 36 t line-haul, and the claim scope could not be read. This is the highest-priority document to re-check with real database access before any S3 novelty position is asserted.

items.name: US8448730B2 — Multi-axle hybrid drive system for a vehicle (ZF Friedrichshafen AG; inventors Muller, Borntrager)
items.what_it_claims: Multi-axle hybrid drive, discussed in the context of wheel-hub motors on articulated buses to distribute drive power advantageously between the front coach and the trailer section.
items.architecture: Multi-axle hybrid with distributed electric drive (heavy passenger vehicle)
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS only. Confirms ZF's presence in split-axle heavy hybrid drive but does not reach fixed-ratio engine drive. Listed because ZF was a named assignee to sweep and this is the substantive ZF hit.

items.name: US20090223725A1 — Hybrid electric conversion kit for rear-wheel drive, all wheel drive, and four wheel drive vehicles
items.what_it_claims: Conversion-kit hybridisation; states that heavy-duty MULTIPLE-DRIVEN-AXLE trucks may be hybridised with an electric motor placed BEFORE, BETWEEN, OR AFTER the rear axles, the motor adding torque on controller command.
items.architecture: Retrofit through-the-road / in-driveline hybrid on a heavy tandem
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS. A published, dated disclosure that placing an electric motor at one of the rear tandem axles of a heavy truck is a known option — further evidence the tandem-split topology is public.

items.name: Tandem-axle and e-axle DISCONNECT cluster — US11155160 (disconnect clutch for a tandem axle assembly); US20200215907A1 (disconnect mechanism for a tandem axle system); US9656545 / US20150072826A1 (tandem axle disconnect with synchronized overdrive); US10857881 (electric drivetrain for a tandem drive axle, with axle disconnect clutch); US8562479B2 / WO2008019759A1 / DE102006045007A1 (tandem axle with two drivable axles and a partially deactivatable driveline); US6793034B2 (wheel-end and center axle disconnects for an electric or HEV); US11274735 / US11674575 (drive axle with a disconnect device); US12409727 (differential-disconnect electric axle, engaged/disengaged on state of charge); US11794714 (sensorless driveline-disconnect control and diagnostic)
items.what_it_claims: Collectively: selectively connecting/disconnecting one driven axle of a tandem from the other; inter-axle differential plus clutching assembly; disconnecting the rear axle(s) of a tandem for fuel economy with a synchronized overdrive; an e-axle motor-generator engaged to first and second drive axle assemblies via a Cardan shaft with a controller-commanded axle disconnect clutch; decoupling motors and driveline components from the wheels to cut non-conservative (friction/churning) losses so range and efficiency improve without hurting performance; disengaging one drive axle during CRUISE specifically to cut friction losses.
items.architecture: Mechanical and electrical axle-disconnect hardware and control for heavy tandems and e-axles
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND (no loss figures retrievable through this channel)
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES S3's 'disconnectable e-axle' element completely and from many suppliers. S3 gets no novelty from the disconnect itself, and — more usefully for WS8 — the existence and commercial breadth of this art means the spin-drag deletion S3 assumes is a REAL, PURCHASABLE capability rather than a modelling convenience. It also means the disconnect's own actuator mass, control complexity and failure modes are well-documented obligations S3 must carry, not ignore.

items.name: US6481519B1 / US6499549B2 / US6604591B2 — Electric drive axle for hybrid vehicle; Drive axle for hybrid vehicle; Electric drive motor axle with integrated reduction and differential gearset
items.what_it_claims: An electric drive axle in which an electric motor drives a compact gearbox comprising a planetary reduction unit and a differential assembly; when used with a conventional ENGINE-BASED powertrain on the other set of wheels, the electric drive axle establishes a through-the-road four-wheel-drive hybrid. The ICE is the first drive source to a first set of wheels and the e-axle the second drive source to a second set.
items.architecture: P4 e-axle, single-stage planetary reduction, paired with a conventional engine axle
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: OCCUPIES the basic single-reduction e-axle-plus-engine-axle building block from around 2000-2003. Together with EP0492152A1 this closes the door on any claim to the bare S3 topology; it says nothing about deleting the engine axle's gearbox.

items.name: US12539861 / EP4331885 — Software-defined hybrid powertrain and vehicle (LCB International Inc; inventors Gesang Wangjie, Cha Wei)
items.what_it_claims: Software/hardware decoupling of a hybrid powertrain such that the instantaneous operating point of the powertrain OUTPUT SHAFT and the instantaneous operating point of the ENGINE have a many-to-many bidirectional mapping — one output point can correspond to different engine points and vice versa — so that road-load power control and engine power control are essentially independent, and the powertrain's performance metrics are substantially independent of the engine, motor and pack performance.
items.architecture: Hybrid powertrain framed as decoupling engine operating point from road load in software
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: NEIGHBOURS at the level of PRINCIPLE and is very recent. S3's justification for deleting the gearbox is precisely that the e-axle decouples the engine's operating point from road load. A live filing asserting that decoupling as the invention is a claim-scope risk worth checking properly, even though the embodiment is not a fixed-ratio tandem-split Class 8.

items.name: US7572201B2 / US20070093341A1 — Electric hybrid powertrain system
items.what_it_claims: Hybrid electric powertrain with an engine plus motor and motor-generator subsystem using MULTIPLE-RATIO GEARING in the forward-drive power flow path, providing two forward driving speed ratios, expressly to improve powertrain GRADEABILITY and to supply the increased traction-wheel and REVERSE drive torque required for heavy-duty vehicle and truck powertrains.
items.architecture: Heavy-duty hybrid with deliberately added multi-ratio gearing
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND
items.relevance_to_S3: CONTRADICTS the S3 premise directly and is filed for exactly S3's vehicle class. Its stated problem — heavy-duty forward gradeability and reverse torque — is what a single fixed ratio cannot serve, and its solution is more ratios. See contradictions.

items.name: Meritor / heavy e-axle multi-ratio cluster — US11054009 and US11460096 ('Single electric motor drive axle with multiple ratios'); US12203544 and US9809098 (two-speed transmission for electric vehicle); US12385551 (motor-gearbox arrangement)
items.what_it_claims: Electric drive axles for heavy vehicles built with a single motor but TWO or THREE speeds; background states that current e-axle designs add components — extra motors, a multi-speed gearbox between motor and axle, and hub reduction — specifically to reach the desired overall axle ratio and performance.
items.architecture: Heavy-duty e-axle with multi-speed gearing between motor and axle
items.quantified_result: NONE FOUND in patent text; supporting literature (heavy-duty e-truck transmission ratio optimisation studies) reports that a single-speed heavy e-drive gives good low-speed torque and gradeability OR high top speed but not both, and that a 3-speed meets gradeability at lowest energy consumption for heavy trucks.
items.relevance_to_S3: CONTRADICTS S3's axle B as configured by WS8. S3's e-axle is a single 12.0:1 reduction, ratio-pinned by WS2's 7,200 rpm rotor limit, and is simultaneously asked to own launch of a 36.3 t combination AND to keep up to 105 km/h plus downhill overspeed. The commercial heavy e-axle world resolves that same conflict with two or three speeds. See contradictions.

contradictions.claim: One fixed ratio can serve a Class 8 engine path, because the e-axle covers the low end — i.e. the change-speed gearbox is deletable on a 36.3 t combination.
contradictions.evidence: Dana Heavy Vehicle's own commercial-vehicle hybrid family states the governing constraint in its background: commercial vehicles have the unique demand of needing 'a low speed, high torque mode of operation while also having a high speed, low torque mode of operation', and that this is what makes hybridising commercial drivetrains hard. Dana's answer, in the title of the patent, is DUAL RANGE DISCONNECT AXLES — it adds ratios to the axles rather than removing them from the driveline. This is the largest heavy-axle supplier, with 2015 priority, stating that two operating regimes are a requirement of the vehicle class and solving it with more ratios, not one.

contradictions.claim: A fixed-ratio engine drive plus an electric machine is a sufficient ratio set.
contradictions.evidence: The Paice/Severinsky family — the very disclosure that originated 'engine at a fixed ratio, no variable-ratio transmission, motor for low speed, engine for cruise' — itself provides in its continuations that 'a two-speed transmission may further be provided, TO FURTHER BROADEN THE VEHICLE'S LOAD RANGE', and separately adds a turbocharger activated when load exceeds engine maximum torque for an extended period. The authors of the fixed-ratio idea found one ratio insufficient for load range on a passenger car of roughly 1.5 t. S3 proposes the same single-ratio bet at 36,300 kg GCW, a load-range problem larger by more than an order of magnitude, and on a duty cycle that includes a sustained 6% grade.

contradictions.claim: S3's axle B — a single-speed e-axle at 12.0:1 — can own launch of a 36.3 t combination and also run to 105 km/h plus downhill overspeed.
contradictions.evidence: Meritor's own heavy e-axle filings are titled 'Single electric motor drive axle with MULTIPLE RATIOS' and state in background that current electric drive axle designs deliberately add a multi-speed gearbox between motor and axle plus a hub reduction to reach the required overall ratio and performance. The supporting engineering literature is explicit that a one-speed heavy e-drive cannot provide both high torque on slopes and high speed on the flat, and that for heavy trucks a 3-speed meets gradeability at the lowest energy consumption. S3's ratio is not chosen for the duty at all — WS8's own code comment says 12.0:1 is pinned by WS2's carried 7,200 rpm rotor limit and that 'a numerically higher ratio would buy startability but would over-speed WS2's rotor'. That is an admission on the record that S3's launch ratio is set by a borrowed component constraint rather than by the launch requirement.

contradictions.claim: Heavy-duty gradeability and reverse can be met without multi-ratio gearing in the mechanical path.
contradictions.evidence: US7572201B2 / US20070093341A1 ('Electric hybrid powertrain system') is a heavy-duty hybrid filing whose stated purpose is to add multiple-ratio gearing giving two forward driving speed ratios expressly to improve powertrain GRADEABILITY and to supply the increased traction-wheel torque and REVERSE drive torque 'required for heavy-duty vehicle and truck powertrains'. Reverse is a duty S3's architecture assigns entirely to axle B; the reference treats reverse torque as a named heavy-duty requirement that motivated adding ratios rather than removing them.

contradictions.claim: Once the engine's mechanical path is fixed-ratio, the vehicle needs no gearbox anywhere — including on the electric side.
contradictions.evidence: Hyliion's own Hypertruck ERX, the most directly comparable Class 8 product, drives its tandem with two Meritor 14Xe e-axles each having its own TWO-SPEED gearbox — in a vehicle that has no engine mechanical path at all and therefore had every commercial incentive to be single-speed. A purpose-built Class 8 electric tandem, unconstrained by any diesel, still bought two speeds per axle. S3 asserts 'no gearbox ANYWHERE' on a vehicle that is heavier in mission and has an additional fixed-ratio diesel constraint.

contradictions.claim: The tandem split is benign for traction — putting all diesel tractive effort through ONE axle of the tandem is a modelling detail.
contradictions.evidence: Hyliion filed specifically on traction assistance (US20240034298A1): predicting slip conditions along a route from vehicle, load and external/cloud data, including previous slip events, and reconfiguring the electric drive powertrain in anticipation. A company operating split-drive Class 8 tractors in the field found single-axle slip enough of a live problem to patent a predictive countermeasure. Separately, the tandem-disconnect art (US9656545, US8562479) exists because running a heavy tandem in single-axle mode is a deliberate, conditional, controller-managed state — not a default. S3's Task 5 'diesel-axle-only adhesion on cruise grades' risk is therefore a real, industry-recognised failure mode, not a formality.

contradictions.claim: The heavy-duty tandem-split hybrid can be built with the engine on a fixed ratio.
contradictions.evidence: BAE Systems' US8875819B2 is the closest structural analogue found — engine as PRIMARY motive power to the front-most and middle drive axles, clutched electric motor to the rear-most drive axle, filed 2010 for medium/heavy duty. Even in this deliberate tandem-split heavy-duty design the engine is retained as the primary conventional motive path, with no indication that its change-speed transmission was removed. Every heavy-duty split-axle document located in this sweep — BAE, Dana, MAN DE102016006206A1, EP0812720A1 (which names a 'switchable transmission' on the engine axle explicitly), Scania WO2019165167A1 (whose entire invention is patching gear-shift torque holes) — keeps a multi-ratio transmission on the engine path. That is six independent heavy-vehicle actors over thirty years converging on the same choice S3 proposes to reverse.

contradictions.claim: Deleting the gearbox is where the fuel savings are on a Class 8 through-the-road hybrid.
contradictions.evidence: Hyliion's published product accounting for the 6X4HE attributes 30% total savings as 15% hybrid drive axle + 12% APU + 3% aerodynamics — i.e. the e-axle overlay on a COMPLETELY UNMODIFIED diesel-plus-AMT driveline already delivers the drive-axle share, with the gearbox left in place. That sets an uncomfortable bar: S3 must show that removing the transmission adds enough on top of a plain e-axle overlay to justify losing launch capability, grade hold, reverse and limp-home from the mechanical path. WS8's advance gate is >=3% versus S0 at nominal and >=0% at every corner; nothing in the patent record suggests the gearbox deletion is worth more than the risks it creates.

open_ground: EVIDENCE-QUALITY CAVEAT, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT BOUNDS EVERYTHING BELOW: no independent claim was read verbatim. patents.google.com, worldwide.espacenet.com, freepatentsonline.com, image-ppubs.uspto.gov, patents.justia.com, lens.org, api.patentsview.org, developer.uspto.gov and ped.uspto.gov ALL returned 403 connect_rejected from the organisation's egress proxy, to both WebFetch and curl. Only server-side WebSearch worked. Every claim characterisation here is a paraphrase of a search summary. Treat this as a LEAD LIST. Under the program's own verbatim-verification rule this does not clear an FTO or a novelty position, and the Task 0 deliverable should say so on its face rather than presenting these as verified claim readings.

OPEN: no document was found claiming, at Class 8 / 36 t combination scale, an engine driving ONE axle of a TANDEM through a SINGLE FIXED RATIO with NO change-speed gearbox anywhere in the vehicle, jointly with a disconnectable e-axle on the OTHER tandem axle owning launch, low speed, regen and peak assist. The two halves are each well occupied but at different scales: fixed-ratio/no-gearbox with electric launch exists on light vehicles (US5343970 expired, US9663101 Audi, US8695738, US7470215); heavy-duty tandem split exists with the gearbox retained (US8875819 BAE, Dana WO2017100258 family, EP0812720, MAN DE102016006206A1, Hyliion TTR family). The junction is the open ground — and the contradictions above are the reason it is open.

OPEN: rev-matched engagement of a fixed-ratio engine drive is claimed as a bare mechanism (US9005077: over-speed the engine past the fixed engine-speed-to-axle-speed ratio, then close the selectable clutch), but NOT the cross-axle version S3 needs — using the SECOND axle's electric machine to hold vehicle speed and torque steady while the first axle's fixed-ratio clutch is synchronised and closed on a loaded heavy combination. Nothing was found combining rev-match, tandem split and heavy-duty scale. This is the most defensible narrow claim S3 could support, and it is also the element WS8 must actually model: the engagement transient at 36 t is where a fixed-ratio clutch either works or destroys itself.

OPEN: nothing was found assigning creep, low-speed manoeuvring, dock work and reverse WHOLLY to the e-axle while the fixed-ratio engine axle stays declutched below a threshold, on a heavy combination. Note that US7572201B2 names heavy-duty REVERSE drive torque as a reason to ADD ratios, so this open ground is open partly because others judged it unworkable, not merely unexplored.

OPEN AND UNSOLVED, NOT MERELY UNCLAIMED: e-axle-fault limp-home. With no gearbox on the diesel axle, a failed or disconnected axle B leaves the vehicle with no launch capability at all — a fixed-ratio diesel cannot start a 36.3 t combination from rest. No patent was found addressing degraded-mode operation of a transmissionless fixed-ratio engine axle. The absence of art here should be read as a warning rather than an opportunity: this is a single-point-of-failure immobilisation mode that a fleet operator will price, and WS8's Task 5 sensitivity on e-axle-fault limp capability is the place it has to be confronted honestly.

OPEN: no patent or filing was found reporting quantified fuel energy per PAYLOAD tonne-km for a transmissionless tandem-split Class 8. Quantified results are essentially absent across the patent corpus generally (NONE FOUND on nearly every item). The only usable external numbers are product-level and vendor-sourced: Hyliion's 15% drive-axle share of a 30% total, and ePower's unverified 50-65% specification assertion against a stated 5.5 mpg / <=38% driveline baseline. Neither is a calibration source. WS8's S0 must be calibrated to the public reference band the assignment names, not to any of these.

SEARCHED AND FOUND NOTHING — explicit negative results, since these define the open ground. (1) No single-fixed-ratio ENGINE axle claim on a commercial vehicle from any of: Eaton, Cummins, Volvo, Scania, ZF, Bosch, Daimler/Mercedes, PACCAR, Allison, BorgWarner, Nikola or Tesla. Substantive hits from these names were all multi-ratio, P2/P3 driveline-mounted, or e-axle-only. (2) No claim phrased as 'wherein the vehicle does not include a change-speed transmission' or equivalent on a heavy vehicle — searched in that literal form and in paraphrase. (3) German-language sweep (Verbrennungsmotor / feste Uebersetzung / ohne Schaltgetriebe / Nutzfahrzeug / Anfahren) returned only gearbox-retaining architectures; the one useful find was EP0492152A1's recital of the through-the-road split as ALREADY KNOWN in 1991. (4) Chinese-language sweep returned CN115416473A as the only heavy multi-axle filing with explicit gearbox elimination, and that is an off-highway engineering vehicle. (5) No Hyliion filing was found that touches the transmission at all — the entire portfolio is predicated on leaving the primary drivetrain alone. (6) No academic or patent document was found proposing single-fixed-ratio diesel drive on a line-haul tractor.

FREEDOM-TO-OPERATE READING (provisional, unverified). The bare S3 TOPOLOGY is almost certainly unencumbered: through-the-road engine-on-one-axle / electric-on-the-other was admitted prior art in EP0492152A1 in 1991, US5343970's fixed-ratio-plus-electric-launch concept has EXPIRED, and single-reduction e-axle-plus-engine-axle appears in US6481519B1 around 2000. The live exposure is not topology but CONTROL and CONTINUATIONS: the later Paice members, Audi US9663101's electric-launch-to-threshold-speed control, Scania WO2019165167A1's cross-axle torque compensation, LCB US12539861's operating-point-decoupling framing, and the Dana and Hyliion families' controller claims. Any S3 control software should be cleared against those specifically.

RECOMMENDATION TO THE LEAD, stated plainly because the sweep points one way. The patent record does not merely fail to anticipate S3 — it documents six independent heavy-vehicle actors over thirty years arriving at the opposite choice, and it documents the fixed-ratio idea's own originators adding a second ratio for load range on a vehicle 1/24th of S3's mass. The open ground is real but it is open for a reason that WS8 can test directly in physics rather than in prior art: the fixed-ratio grade-hold floor, the diesel-axle-only adhesion limit on cruise grades, and the single-speed e-axle's launch-versus-top-speed conflict at a ratio pinned by WS2's rotor limit. Task 0 should hand those three to Task 5 as pre-identified kill mechanisms, not as generic sensitivities. Prior art has told us where S3 breaks; the trial should go looking there first.

lens: COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS AND PROGRAMS — Class 7/8 hybrid and electrified-overlay powertrains that were real products or funded programs, scored on (a) architecture class, (b) claimed fuel saving + test basis, (c) added mass, (d) WHETHER THE ICE KEPT A MULTI-SPEED TRANSMISSION. Headline result: across ~35 products/programs on four continents and 30 years, the number of on-highway Class 8 vehicles in which a combustion engine drove the road wheels through a single fixed ratio with no gearbox anywhere is ZERO. Every parallel/overlay product kept the AMT untouched; every product that DID delete the AMT (Hyliion Hypertruck ERX, ePower, ReVolt, Edison, Wrightspeed, BAE, ProPulse) did so by going SERIES — mechanically decoupling the engine entirely — and then still fitted 2-, 3- or 5-speed gearboxes on the traction side. S3's specific novelty (mechanical fixed-ratio diesel axle + disconnectable e-axle owning launch) is genuinely unoccupied ground; the S3 hazard is not novelty but the two things the industry paid gearboxes to buy: launch torque at 36.3 t and engine-speed decoupling from road speed. PROVENANCE CAVEAT: this environment blocks all direct HTTPS egress (WebFetch and curl return EGRESS_BLOCKED/403 for every host tried, including wikipedia, sec.gov, patents.google.com, nacfe.org, OEM sites). Every datum below comes from server-side WebSearch result summaries with the source URL attached; primary-document verification of any load-bearing number is NOT possible in this session and should be flagged provisional per E13 precedent.

items.name: Hyliion 6X4HE Hybrid Electric System
items.what_it_claims: Bolt-on/retrofit hybrid drive axle for Class 8 tractors: 115 hp / 1,500 lb-ft (86 kW / 2,034 Nm) motorized axle + Li-ion pack + controller that captures regen downhill and re-applies it uphill to hold the diesel at its efficient rpm; also runs a 10-hour 18,000 BTU idle-free APU. Announced 2017, wound down with the rest of Hyliion's powertrain business Q1-2024.
items.architecture: P4 / through-the-road overlay on the tractor's own tandem. Replaces a 6x2 dead axle (or adds to a 4x2) to make a 6x4 — the diesel keeps driving its own axle; the electric machine drives the other tandem axle. This is the ONLY commercial 'tandem split' ever built.
items.quantified_result: 15% fuel saving from the hybrid axle alone, stated best-case in rolling hilly terrain; 30% total only when stacked with 12% APU + 3% aero. Mass: +800 lb (363 kg) after the axle swap-out, net +400 lb (181 kg) against the federal 400 lb APU allowance. Price $37,000-$40,000 for the earlier trailer version, ~2-yr payback at $2.50/gal. Battery capacity never disclosed in kWh (described only as a '300 amp' pack).
items.relevance_to_S3: DIRECT PRECEDENT AND DIRECT WARNING. It is S3's tandem topology minus S3's premise: Hyliion kept the diesel's AMT completely untouched and used the e-axle purely as an overlay, never as the launch owner. Its honest hybrid-only number (15%, best-case terrain) is the empirical ceiling for a tandem-split overlay — and it was earned WITH the AMT still doing the launch and ratio work S3 proposes to delete. Also: the 400 lb APU exemption is the only weight relief an overlay gets, which matters for WS8's payload tonne-km metric.

items.name: Hyliion Hybrid electric-drive TRAILER tandem (the 6X4HE's predecessor)
items.what_it_claims: Hyliion's first product (2016-2017): a complete replacement trailer tandem — axles, suspension, brakes, motor — that captures braking/downhill energy and reapplies it to help the tractor launch and climb.
items.architecture: Through-the-road / P4 on the TRAILER (electrified-trailer overlay). No mechanical connection to the tractor powertrain at all.
items.quantified_result: 21% claimed for the electric-drive tandem alone in early 2016 development; later revised down to 10-20% from hybrid operation alone. System cost $37,000-$40,000; ~2-year payback at $2.50/gal diesel.
items.relevance_to_S3: Shows the lineage: the claimed number fell from 21% -> 15% as the product moved from concept to a tractor-mounted axle and got measured. Any S3 overlay-derived expectation should be discounted the same way. Confirms that from the very first product, the tractor's engine + AMT were left entirely alone.

items.name: Hyliion Hypertruck ERX (Peterbilt 579)
items.what_it_claims: Class 8 series-hybrid: natural-gas engine drives a generator only; batteries drive e-axles. 75 mi battery-only range for CARB ZEV credit, up to ~1,000-1,300 mi total on one CNG fill. Dana motor/inverter/axle technology, Cummins ISX12G/ISX12N genset, 670 hp. Discontinued Nov-2023 / Q1-2024.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid. Engine mechanically decoupled — the generator is bolted to the rear of the engine LITERALLY WHERE THE TRANSMISSION USED TO BE. Tandem e-axles (Meritor 14Xe), each with its own motor.
items.quantified_result: 211 kWh total battery (two packs); 670 hp at the axles; 75 mi electric range; up to 1,000+ mi combined. Each of the two 14Xe drive axles carries a TWO-SPEED gearbox.
items.relevance_to_S3: THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING ITEM. This is the only production-intent Class 8 on-highway truck that actually deleted the AMT — and it still needed two two-speed axle gearboxes to move 36 t. 'No gearbox anywhere' was not achievable even when the engine was fully decoupled and free to sit at its best point. Also a commercial cautionary tale: killed for complexity, cost, and CARB engine recertification, not for physics.

items.name: Revoy EV dolly (Revoy EV / plug-in electric dolly)
items.what_it_claims: A self-contained battery + e-axle dolly that hitches between an unmodified diesel tractor and its trailer in <5 min, with swap hubs on the corridor. Explicitly requires NO modification to the truck or trailer; reads the existing air and electrical lines and a smart kingpin. Raised $27M July-2026.
items.architecture: Through-the-road overlay inserted in the coupling — a P4 the tractor doesn't even know about. Single-speed e-axle.
items.quantified_result: 525-575 kWh LFP, 400 kW motor, ~200-250 mi (320-400 km) of electric range hauling a loaded 36 t rig. Claimed diesel reduction up to 90-95% (MVTS measured 90.4% on flat terrain), emissions -85%, effective 6-8 mpg -> ~120 mpg diesel-equivalent, ~$25,000/yr fuel saving. MASS: ~10 t / ~22,000 lb, and it adds ~13 ft of length.
items.relevance_to_S3: Two lessons. (1) The huge headline savings are ENERGY SUBSTITUTION (grid kWh displacing diesel), not powertrain efficiency — WS8 must not benchmark S3's thermodynamic gains against numbers like these. (2) A ~10 t overlay is catastrophic in fuel-energy-per-PAYLOAD-tonne-km terms and none of the marketing charges it. This is exactly the accounting failure the WS8 metric of record exists to prevent.

items.name: Range Energy RA-01 / RB-01 powered trailer (eTrailer)
items.what_it_claims: A 53-ft dry van/reefer whose own axle is electrified and which senses tractor push/pull through an instrumented 'smart kingpin', so it propels itself and unloads the tractor. Winter-validated April-2026; customer deliveries targeted by end of 2026.
items.architecture: Through-the-road / P4 trailer overlay. 800 V single-speed e-axle. Tractor powertrain and AMT completely untouched.
items.quantified_result: 200 kWh (RA-01) or 200/300 kWh (RB-01); 250-350 kW; up to 14,000 Nm (10,326 lb-ft) at the wheels. MVT Solutions certified test: +36.3% fuel economy (3.82 mpg with system on vs off); company-reported 36.9%, 48% on a heavily loaded city cycle, 41% mixed, LOWER on long-haul. RB-01 initial tests 47-67% mpg improvement = 32-40% fuel COST reduction. Fleet operations claim 50-70% fuel-economy improvement.
items.relevance_to_S3: Best-documented single-speed Class 8 e-axle torque number in the record: 14,000 Nm at the wheel. That is the concrete yardstick for whether an S3 e-axle can own launch — see the contradiction entry on startability, where 36.3 t on a 20% grade needs ~36,600 Nm at 0.50 m rolling radius. Also note the explicit statement that the gains are LOWEST on long-haul, the very cycle WS8 Task 1(a) targets.

items.name: Trailer Dynamics / KRONE eTrailer
items.what_it_claims: European electrified semitrailer, orderable from KRONE since 2024, that drives and recuperates to cut the tractor's diesel and CO2.
items.architecture: Through-the-road / P4 trailer overlay, LFP batteries, e-axle. Tractor unmodified.
items.quantified_result: eAxle 360 kW continuous / 580 kW peak. Claimed average 40% diesel and CO2 reduction. Trailer Dynamics raised EUR 25M on a 'cuts fuel use by 40%' claim.
items.relevance_to_S3: Third independent confirmation that the entire commercial e-overlay industry (Hyliion, Revoy, Range, Trailer Dynamics) has converged on: leave the tractor's engine and AMT alone, put a SINGLE-SPEED e-axle somewhere behind the fifth wheel. Nobody has monetised AMT deletion — which is precisely the credit S3 is banking on.

items.name: Allison eGen Power 100D / 130D e-axle
items.what_it_claims: Fully integrated Class 7/8 electric drive axle for vehicles up to ~36 t GVW (100D, 10.4 t / 23,000 lb GAWR) and 13 t GAWR (130D, EU/APAC).
items.architecture: Primary-drive e-axle (BEV traction), dual motor, WITH AN INTEGRATED TWO-SPEED GEARBOX in the central housing plus diff lock.
items.quantified_result: >450 kW continuous, 650 kW peak; 130D max 47,000 Nm at the wheels. Allison's own stated rationale for the two-speed: 'enabling the high torque required to get heavy loads moving, while also offering superior efficiency at cruise speed.'
items.relevance_to_S3: Allison states S3's exact design tension in one sentence and resolves it with a gearbox. Their answer to 'launch torque AND cruise efficiency from one machine' is two ratios, on a machine that only has to do the electric half of S3's job.

items.name: Cummins/Accelera-Meritor 14Xe and 17Xe ePowertrain
items.what_it_claims: Modular e-axles built on the Meritor 14X/17X housings for medium and heavy duty; 17Xe supports 44 t GCW in 4x2/6x2.
items.architecture: Primary-drive e-axle. Offered SINGLE-, TWO- or THREE-SPEED — the multi-speed dual-countershaft box is the option that gets specified for heavy work. 14Xe is what Hyliion used, in two-speed form.
items.quantified_result: 17Xe: 420 kW continuous / 450 kW peak, 44 t GCW capability, range of ratios and up to three-speed. 14Xe: 150/180/200 kW continuous, 250 kW peak, Class 6-7 duty. The transmission is a removable module (can be pulled without touching the HV system).
items.relevance_to_S3: Quantifies the duty split S3 assumes: a 150-250 kW single-speed-capable axle is a Class 6-7 device; moving 44 t wants 420-450 kW and up to three ratios. If S3's e-axle must launch 36.3 t alone, it is in 17Xe territory, i.e. the multi-speed end of the catalogue — and its mass must be charged accordingly.

items.name: ZF AxTrax 2 / AxTrax 2 dual
items.what_it_claims: Second-generation ZF commercial-vehicle electric axle platform; the 'dual' variant is explicitly the heavy-duty Class 8 offering.
items.architecture: Primary-drive e-axle with an INTEGRATED THREE-SPEED TRANSMISSION in both single- and dual-motor variants.
items.quantified_result: AxTrax 2 single: 210 kW continuous, 25,980 Nm (19,162 lb-ft) peak, three-speed. AxTrax 2 dual (Class 8): 380 kW continuous, 54,800 Nm (40,418 lb-ft) peak, two motors, two inverters, THREE-SPEED.
items.relevance_to_S3: The strongest single contradiction of 'no gearbox anywhere'. The largest supplier in the segment, designing a clean-sheet Class 8 axle in the 2020s with no legacy constraint, chose THREE ratios. The 54,800 Nm figure is only reachable through those ratios.

items.name: Dana Spicer Electrified Zero-8 e-Axles / eS9000r
items.what_it_claims: Class 7/8 e-axle family in 4x2, 6x2 and 6x4 based on the proven Spicer S110/S111/S130 platforms; supplied the motor/inverter/axle technology into Hyliion's Hypertruck ERX.
items.architecture: Primary-drive e-axle, explicitly described as MULTI-SPEED for Class 7/8. Includes an electronically controlled parking pawl 'which is an important feature for vehicles without a traditional transmission'.
items.quantified_result: Zero-8 family covers 4x2/6x2/6x4 multi-speed Class 7-8 architectures; eS9000r (Class 4-5) is fully integrated including gearbox and motor.
items.relevance_to_S3: A second-order but real S3 finding: Dana had to add a parking pawl because deleting the transmission also deletes the park/hold function. S3's 'no gearbox anywhere' silently deletes park lock, neutral, and reverse — reverse in particular must come entirely from the e-axle, and the fixed-ratio diesel axle is dragged backwards through its clutch.

items.name: Bosch commercial-vehicle eAxle (Nikola Class 8 partnership)
items.what_it_claims: Scalable modular eAxle integrating motor, power electronics and TRANSMISSION in one unit; co-developed with Nikola as 'the world's first true dual-motor commercial-vehicle eAxle for a long-haul truck'.
items.architecture: Primary-drive e-axle, dual motor, integrated transmission.
items.quantified_result: Bosch eAxle platform spans 50-300 kW and 1,000-6,000 Nm at the module; the Nikola Class 8 application targets >1,000 hp and 2,000 lb-ft (2,711 Nm) at the input.
items.relevance_to_S3: Confirms the supplier consensus that a heavy e-axle is motor + power electronics + GEARBOX as an inseparable unit. There is no Class 8 supplier offering a gearless direct-drive axle for either an ICE or an e-machine.

items.name: Scania hybrid and plug-in hybrid trucks (DC09 + 130 kW machine; GE281 gearbox)
items.what_it_claims: Production European hybrid and PHEV trucks for urban/regional duty; the electric machine is merged into the Opticruise gearbox itself.
items.architecture: P2 pre-transmission parallel. The GE281 couples two electric machines into essential parts of the 2020-generation Opticruise gearbox — i.e. the AMT is not merely retained, it is the structural host for the hybrid.
items.quantified_result: DC09 diesel + 130 kW (177 hp) electric machine; up to 40% fuel saving claimed, explicitly IN CITY AREAS, and explicitly conditional on route hilliness and stop count.
items.relevance_to_S3: The most direct OEM rebuttal of AMT deletion: Scania's engineering answer was to build the hybrid INTO the gearbox. And the honest framing of the claim (40% urban, degrading with fewer stops) is the pattern WS8 should expect for any line-haul candidate.

items.name: Volvo I-SAM / Volvo FE Hybrid (4th-generation Volvo Group hybrid)
items.what_it_claims: Production heavy parallel hybrid: combined starter/drive motor/alternator plus ECU, batteries charged by the diesel and by braking.
items.architecture: P2 parallel, and I-SAM 'interacts with' and RETAINS the I-Shift automated gearshift system.
items.quantified_result: Headline 'up to 35%'; realistic figures 15-20% for distribution and refuse depending on chassis and cycle; up to 30% for refuse operators with an electrified compactor.
items.relevance_to_S3: Second OEM data point that the AMT stays. The spread between the 35% headline and the 15-20% duty-cycle reality is the discount factor WS8 should apply to any single-number hybrid claim in the literature.

items.name: Volvo Concept Truck — long-haul hybrid powertrain (2016-2017)
items.what_it_claims: Volvo's own attempt at exactly WS8's use case: a heavy hybrid for LONG-HAUL, with I-See topography look-ahead choosing between diesel and motor, recovering energy on slopes steeper than 1%.
items.architecture: Parallel hybrid retaining I-Shift; up to 10 km of full-electric running.
items.quantified_result: HYBRID PATH ALONE: 5-10% fuel saving, by shutting the engine off for up to 30% of driving time. The famous '30%' figure is the whole vehicle including aero and other measures, not the hybrid.
items.relevance_to_S3: The cleanest OEM-stated ceiling for a line-haul hybrid: 5-10%, from the company that built and ran one, with topography-optimal control. S3 must beat S0 by >=3% at nominal AND >=0% at every corner while carrying an e-axle, a pack, and a fixed-ratio penalty — inside a 5-10% total envelope. That is the margin WS8 is fighting for.

items.name: DOE SuperTruck II — Volvo
items.what_it_claims: DOE-funded Class 8 line-haul demonstrator; goal 100% freight-efficiency improvement over a 2009 baseline.
items.architecture: Conventional diesel + AMT with a 48 V MICRO-hybrid (integrated starter-generator) for accessories and hotel loads only. No traction hybridization.
items.quantified_result: 134% freight-efficiency improvement (goal was 100%); >12 mpg; tested on real roads with traffic and elevation at 65,000 lb GCVWR (note: NOT 80,000 lb).
items.relevance_to_S3: With federal money and a clean sheet, Volvo declined to hybridize the traction path at all and declined to touch the transmission. Also a calibration warning for WS8 Task 2: SuperTruck mpg headlines are frequently at 65,000 lb, not at 80,000 lb / 36.3 t.

items.name: DOE SuperTruck II — Daimler / Freightliner
items.what_it_claims: Class 8 line-haul demonstrator with split cooling, two-stage turbocharging, 48 V system and an extreme downsped driveline.
items.architecture: Conventional diesel + multi-speed AMT + 48 V electrical. DOWNSPED DRIVELINE WITH A 1.75:1 AXLE RATIO GIVING 950 rpm AT HIGHWAY CRUISE.
items.quantified_result: 12 mpg average on test routes; 5.7% fuel-consumption reduction over SuperTruck I; >12% aero drag reduction vs SuperTruck I; 48 V e-HVAC using 50% less energy.
items.relevance_to_S3: THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE NUMBER FOR S3'S CRUISE RATIO. 1.75:1 at 950 rpm cruise is the state of the art in 'as close to a single cruise ratio as anyone dares'. Take it literally as S3's fixed ratio and engine speed falls linearly with road speed: at 30 km/h the diesel would be at roughly 270 rpm — below idle, i.e. mechanically unable to contribute. That is the fixed-ratio trap, expressed in a real OEM number.

items.name: DOE SuperTruck II — Navistar / International (with Bosch)
items.what_it_claims: The only SuperTruck II that hybridized the TRACTION path. Control law as reported: use electric power at stops and for higher launch torque, then 'as the vehicle reaches a specific speed or load, the system switches from electric to diesel operation'.
items.architecture: High-voltage parallel hybrid (Bosch) on an S13 13 L engine, with a multi-speed AMT retained.
items.quantified_result: 150 kW electric motor, 30 kWh battery, S13 13 L diesel; 16 mpg; 170% freight-efficiency improvement vs 2009 baseline; 55% engine brake thermal efficiency.
items.relevance_to_S3: THE CLOSEST ANYONE HAS COME TO S3'S CONTROL LAW — electric owns launch and low speed, diesel takes over above a speed/load threshold — and it was demonstrated on a DOE-funded Class 8 in 2023. Crucially they implemented that control law WITH the AMT still in the truck. So S3's control concept is validated prior art; S3's gearbox deletion is not. This is the item an adjudicator will press hardest on.

items.name: DOE SuperTruck 2 — Kenworth / PACCAR
items.what_it_claims: Class 8 line-haul demonstrator with a mild-hybrid 48 V system driving previously-mechanical accessories (fans, steering, HVAC pumps) and providing engine-off hoteling.
items.architecture: 48 V MILD hybrid (P0-class generator) on a PACCAR MX-11 + TX-12 12-SPEED AUTOMATED TRANSMISSION.
items.quantified_result: 12-12.8 mpg; 136% freight-efficiency improvement vs 2009 T660 (~6 mpg); combination weight cut by >7,000 lb; record 55.7% engine BTE vs ~47% for a modern production diesel.
items.relevance_to_S3: Fourth consecutive DOE-funded clean-sheet Class 8 that kept a 12-speed AMT. Also the best available anchor for WS8's engine map ceiling: 55.7% BTE is a research peak, not a fleet value — Task 2's Willans/BSFC calibration should not be built on it.

items.name: DOE SuperTruck I — Cummins / Peterbilt
items.what_it_claims: First-generation DOE Class 8 demonstrator with exhaust waste-heat recovery and route-aware control software.
items.architecture: Conventional diesel + AMT, no traction hybrid. ISX15-based engine with an exhaust heat recovery system.
items.quantified_result: 10.7 mpg on US-287 Denton-to-Vernon TX; 86% freight-efficiency improvement and 75% fuel-economy improvement over a 24-hour test cycle vs the 2009 baseline.
items.relevance_to_S3: Reference point for WS8 Task 4 (WHR modifier) — the flagship US program that actually fielded exhaust heat recovery on a Class 8, and the mpg it produced on a real public-road route rather than a lab cycle.

items.name: Great Wall Motor Hi4-G hybrid heavy truck
items.what_it_claims: Chinese heavy-truck hybrid launched with 'the world's first 8-speed intelligent hybrid transmission for heavy trucks', marketed as 'three engines, eight gears, ten modes'.
items.architecture: P2 + P2.5 DUAL-MOTOR parallel hybrid with a purpose-built 8-SPEED DHT (dedicated hybrid transmission). Foton-Cummins 13 L 560 hp diesel + two 245 hp motors, ~1,050 hp combined.
items.quantified_result: Comprehensive fuel consumption 29.7 L/100 km vs the 35.8 L/100 km China stage-4 standard for the class = 17% reduction.
items.relevance_to_S3: DECISIVE MARKET EVIDENCE. Given a clean sheet and the world's largest hybrid-HDT market, a manufacturer designed an entirely NEW EIGHT-SPEED gearbox specifically for a heavy hybrid truck. Nobody with commercial skin in the game concluded that hybridization lets you delete ratios; the conclusion was the opposite. Bonus: 29.7 and 35.8 L/100 km are useful external sanity points for WS8's 30-38 L/100 km S0 corridor (note Chinese GCW is 49 t, not 36.3 t).

items.name: Foton Auman EST / GTL Star Edition HEV hybrid heavy trucks
items.what_it_claims: Production Chinese hybrid heavy trucks with four modes: multi-stage energy recovery, 'efficient direct drive', 'motor direct drive', and pure-electric assist. Validated over 12 million km and 256 scenarios.
items.architecture: Series-parallel hybrid with a direct-drive mode — but implemented on top of a multi-speed transmission, not instead of one.
items.quantified_result: 730 hp, 3,900 Nm; +30% acceleration vs conventional; 10% fuel reduction overall, 26% on MOUNTAINOUS routes, 16% on HIGHWAY.
items.relevance_to_S3: The best terrain-resolved hybrid HDT dataset in the commercial record and a direct read on WS8's Task 1 cycles: mountain 26% >> highway 16% >> overall 10%. It says S3's fortunes live or die on the 6% mountain segment, and that the flat 85-105 km/h corridor is where hybrid value collapses.

items.name: Chinese new-energy heavy-truck market (context for the above)
items.what_it_claims: Market-scale evidence of what heavy-duty electrification actually ships.
items.architecture: Mixed BEV / swap / hybrid / REx tractors.
items.quantified_result: ZE heavy trucks and tractor-trailers nearly tripled from ~82,300 (2024) to ~232,000 (2025); NE tractor sales +216% in 2025 with hybrid tractors +213%; tractor-trailers reached ~38% ZE share; diesel share fell to a record-low ~60%.
items.relevance_to_S3: Establishes that the 'no single-fixed-ratio HDT exists' finding is not a small-sample artefact — it holds across a market shipping hundreds of thousands of electrified heavy trucks a year, all of which retain multi-speed gearing.

items.name: Edison Motors BDE-Series semi / logging truck
items.what_it_claims: Canadian diesel-electric heavy truck built by loggers, explicitly modelled on locomotive practice; plug-in capable.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid — the engine drives only a generator, so 'there is no transmission connecting the engine to the wheels'. Two driven e-axles.
items.quantified_result: Logging truck: 280 kWh LFP, two rear e-axles at 250 kW each, Caterpillar C9 genset, ~670 hp at the wheels, ~26,000 lb (same as a comparable diesel rig), 2-3 h on battery before the genset starts. BDE-Series semi: Scania genset up to 500 kW, 110 kWh LMO, 740 V, CDTL 5000 e-axles; heavy-haul peak 1,800 kW / 150,000 lb-ft. Claimed up to 50% fuel saving from own logging field data, with 'up to 70-100%' claimed in plug-in operation.
items.relevance_to_S3: The live counter-example of a genuinely gearbox-free heavy truck — but it gets there by SERIES, i.e. by paying the double-conversion tax S1 pays, and its duty cycle (logging, long descents, huge regen) is the opposite of WS8's line-haul corridor. Its mass parity claim (~26,000 lb) is a useful S1 mass sanity check.

items.name: ReVolt Motors series-hybrid Class 8 retrofit
items.what_it_claims: US (Austin TX) retrofit of Peterbilt 579/379 tractors to series diesel-electric; first fleet customer Page Trucking (5 units + 20 to follow). Also eliminates the need for a separate APU.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid retrofit — 'the engine does not drive the wheels but instead acts as a generator'. 9 L Scania diesel genset.
items.quantified_result: 210 kWh battery; 670 hp and 3,500 lb-ft (4,745 Nm); ~12 mpg claimed; ~40% fuel-cost reduction and ~40% emissions reduction; ~1,200 mi total range, ~100 mi battery-only.
items.relevance_to_S3: The most current commercial embodiment of S1 (2025-2026, in fleet service). Its 210 kWh / 670 hp / 9 L-genset sizing is a direct external cross-check on WS8's S1 component sizing, and its 40% claim is the number S1 will be measured against by any reader.

items.name: ePower Engine Systems series diesel-electric Class 8 retrofit
items.what_it_claims: Retrofits standard 18-wheelers to series diesel-electric explicitly to run the engine at constant rpm and 'eliminate the need for complex heavy truck transmissions'. Stated goal: find the outer limit of Class 8 efficiency using the smallest possible components to move 80,000 lb at highway speed.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid, engine fully decoupled — BUT the traction side used an off-the-shelf FIVE-SPEED AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION.
items.quantified_result: ~35% fuel-consumption reduction claimed. Gen-1: 197 hp four-cylinder John Deere turbodiesel, Marathon generator 128 kW at 1,800 rpm, 150 hp Marathon traction motor, 5-speed automatic, 56 PbC batteries. Later gen: 6.7 L diesel giving 200 hp for steady cruise plus ~200 hp of battery boost for acceleration and grades.
items.relevance_to_S3: THE PUREST TEST OF S3'S PREMISE EVER RUN, AND IT FAILED THE GEARBOX PART. A company whose entire thesis was transmission elimination, with a fully decoupled engine and free choice of motor gearing, still bolted a 5-speed to a 150 hp traction motor to move 80,000 lb. If a decoupled series machine needed five ratios, an S3 e-axle asked to launch 36.3 t from a single ratio is the assumption to attack first.

items.name: Wrightspeed Route 1000 (Mack LR refuse demonstrator)
items.what_it_claims: Turbine-electric series powertrain for Class 8 vocational vehicles, multi-fuel.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid: 80 kW Fulcrum microturbine genset (intercooled, recuperated, ~250 lb) + battery + electric traction. Traction unit is Wrightspeed's 'GTD' — A TWO-SPEED GEARBOX WITH INTEGRATED MOTOR.
items.quantified_result: 80 kW turbine genset; 730 kW regenerative braking; rated to 66,000 lb GVW and 40% grades; turbine ~1/10 the weight of an equivalent piston genset.
items.relevance_to_S3: Third independent series-hybrid Class 8 that deleted the ICE transmission and then reinstated gearing on the electric side (two-speed). The 40% gradeability rating shows what the electric path has to be geared for when it owns launch alone — exactly S3's e-axle duty.

items.name: BAE Systems HybriDrive — Series (transit) and Parallel (heavy trucks)
items.what_it_claims: Two distinct product lines from one supplier, letting the architectures be compared like for like. Series: >3,500 transit buses in service, 'uses no mechanical transmission'. Parallel: for Class 6/7/8 vocational trucks.
items.architecture: HybriDrive Series = series hybrid, no mechanical transmission. HybriDrive Parallel = single electric machine BETWEEN THE ENGINE AND THE TRANSMISSION (P2), transmission retained.
items.quantified_result: Series: up to 50% fuel-economy improvement on transit duty with stop/start and accessory electrification. Parallel: 30% average fuel-economy improvement across standard drive cycles in BAE road tests, BEST between 5 and 20 mph; motor 95-145 hp / 300-400 lb-ft supporting 350-600 hp engines with 750-2,150 lb-ft; 3-5 yr payback.
items.relevance_to_S3: Shows exactly where each architecture wins: gearbox deletion pays only in a 5-20 mph stop-go duty. WS8's line-haul corridor at 85-105 km/h is the opposite regime, and BAE's own segmentation says so.

items.name: Oshkosh ProPulse diesel-electric (HEMTT and commercial heavy vehicles)
items.what_it_claims: Military/commercial heavy-vehicle series hybrid; the diesel drives a large generator that feeds independently driven axle modules, each with its own motor and converter, 'to simplify the transmission of power to the wheels'.
items.architecture: SERIES, modular per-axle electric drive, no mechanical driveline from engine to wheels.
items.quantified_result: Fuel economy improvement up to 20%.
items.relevance_to_S3: The heavy-vehicle series-hybrid benchmark from a defence programme with no cost ceiling: 20%, on a duty cycle far more favourable to hybridization than line-haul. Bounds what S1 can plausibly claim.

items.name: Walmart WAVE (Walmart Advanced Vehicle Experience) with Peterbilt / Capstone / Great Dane
items.what_it_claims: Class 8 tractor-trailer concept, 2014: a range-extending series hybrid whose microturbine stays at optimum rpm while the motor and storage handle acceleration and deceleration.
items.architecture: SERIES hybrid with a Capstone microturbine range extender; carbon-fibre trailer; cab-over layout for a short wheelbase.
items.quantified_result: 45.5 kWh Li-polymer pack (seven Corvus modules); 20% aero drag reduction vs a Peterbilt 386; multi-fuel (diesel, natural gas, biodiesel).
items.relevance_to_S3: Establishes that 'turbine/genset + small buffer + e-drive, no ICE gearbox' was tried at Class 8 scale by a top-3 US shipper and a top-3 OEM in 2014 and never productionised. Its 45.5 kWh buffer is a useful lower bound for S1's buffer-pack sizing debate.

items.name: Scania + DHL EREV (extended-range electric truck, Berlin-Hamburg)
items.what_it_claims: Production-based 40 t electric truck with a fuel-burning generator as a bridge technology while charging infrastructure is built out. 100-day revenue-service trial reported.
items.architecture: Range-extended BEV (series REx): battery-electric driveline plus an onboard generator; engine never drives the wheels.
items.quantified_result: 40 t max, 10.5 m; 230 kW continuous / 295 kW peak drive; 416 kWh battery; 120 kW petrol (later diesel/HVO) generator; up to 800 km range. Measured over ~22,000 km in 100 days: >90% of operation in electric mode, range extender active on only ~8.1% of km; 90% CO2 saving.
items.relevance_to_S3: The best-measured REx heavy truck in the record and the closest external analogue to WS8's S4 (150-200 kW sustainer). Note the genset is 120 kW, BELOW S4's 150-200 kW band, and it still delivered 800 km — evidence that S4's genset can be sized down, saving mass against payload.

items.name: MAHLE integrated range-extender module for heavy electric trucks
items.what_it_claims: A single module combining HV generator, ICE, thermal/fluid management, fuel and AdBlue tanks and aftertreatment, droppable into existing BEV truck platforms. Premiere IAA Transportation, September 2026.
items.architecture: Series range extender for a BEV truck; no mechanical path to the wheels.
items.quantified_result: Generator delivers 110-130 kW to the drive system; >800 km total range (~400 km battery + ~400 km REx); replaces roughly one third of the battery capacity and CUTS VEHICLE WEIGHT BY ~600 kg; ~80% less CO2 than a conventional diesel truck in REx operation.
items.relevance_to_S3: The explicit mass trade S4 needs, from a tier-1: swapping a third of the pack for a 110-130 kW genset is worth ~600 kg of payload back. That is a quantified external anchor for WS8's 'pack mass charged honestly against payload' requirement.

items.name: Horse Powertrain range extender for a Scania electric timber truck
items.what_it_claims: Tier-1 range-extender system supplied into a Scania heavy-duty timber-truck pilot in Sweden, combining Scania's electric driveline with a high-efficiency generator.
items.architecture: Series range extender on a BEV heavy truck.
items.quantified_result: Pilot vehicle in service (announced Dec-2025); detailed ratings not disclosed in accessible sources.
items.relevance_to_S3: Confirms REx-for-heavy-BEV has moved from concept to multiple independent tier-1 supply programmes in 2025-2026, i.e. S4 is the candidate with the strongest and most current commercial momentum behind it.

items.name: Tevva 7.5 t hydrogen range-extended electric truck
items.what_it_claims: Type-approved battery-electric truck with a hydrogen fuel-cell range extender for longer duty days.
items.architecture: Range-extended BEV, fuel-cell extender.
